text.p: Israelis who drop cigarette butts on the street could watch a lot of their money going up in smoke.
Israel's parliament has decided to stomp on litterbugs, giving courts the power to fine people who use pavements as ashtrays as much as $15,000.

"Fines used to be tiny, effectively causing people to continue to litter," Nehama Ronen, director-general of the Environment Ministry, said on Wednesday, a day after parliament approved a long list of pollution penalties.

"Now that the fines are so high, such as up to 50,000 shekels ($15,000) for tins thrown from a car or cigarettes...we have really sharp teeth and can clamp down on this ugly phenomenon," she told Israel Radio.
